stories.headline: 'Wada kursi se bada hai': Srinagar MP to quit NC, targets J&K CM Omar over ideology
stories.bodyText:
BUDGAM: At the entrance of the National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi home’s two large banners at the gate sum up the message he wants to convey. One reads, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other says, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).
Inside the hall, party workers gathered in small groups, discussing the fallout of Mehdi's announcement that he would formally resign from as NC MP at a rally here on November 3 on the death anniversary of his father. One worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that.”
Inside in his room, sitting calmly in his chair, Mehdi insists his decision to part ways with the party is final and there is no going back.
“I have been part of this NC for 24 years. I joined it believing that it stood for autonomy and the rights of the people of J&K. But after the abrogation of 
Article 370
, whatever remnants of autonomy we had were taken away and the party despite getting a strong mandate in the 2024 Assembly elections on the promise of challenging the status quo, failed to honour it,” Mehdi told the TOI, accusing the chief minister 
Omar Abdullah
 of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP, “to the point of submission.”
In the room, hanging on the wall was a large photograph of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, a prominent Shia cleric and Congress leader who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.
“I understand it will be long fight but I am not afraid," he said, hastily added that whenever the NC faced an ideological challenge, it found it tough to defend its position. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) managed, he said, for a brief period, to offer it such a challenge before joining an alliance with the BJP in 2015 reduced party to three members today. “There was also an ideological contest between the NC and the Hurriyat Conference in Jammu and Kashmir for many years. I am not endorsing the Hurriyat Conference as it represented the other extreme. But when it came to ideological contestation, the streets were dominated by the other side, not the National Conference,” he said.
He said people need to replace traditional political forces like NC and PDP and other like them with more potent one having conviction. “The common problem with these two political parties and others like them, is their lack of character. It is what they have in common. People trusted the NC and the PDP. But they delivered the same kind of results,” he added.
Mehdi, who has been critical of the CM and his government, said the chief minister normalised the post-abrogation arrangement through his government, Assembly and other constitutional institutions. “The party began speaking the very language that the BJP wanted people across the country to speak after the abrogation of Article 370,” he said. He said he found further clarity after NC president Farooq Abdullah recently said in an interview that if Mehdi believed what he says he was free to resign from the party.
“Referring to me Dr Abdullah said that if I believed Article 370 could be restored, I was free to move out and get it restored. Effectively, he was saying that he himself did not believe Article 370 could not be restored. This again raises the question, if he does not believe it can be restored constitutionally, why people of Jammu and Kashmir were given the assurance during the poll campaign. In the same interview, he asked me to resign from the party as, in his view, I had become an irritant in the process of normalising the post-abrogation status quo. They wanted me to leave the party because I am questioning their position,” he added.
Mehdi also rejected the claim that the NC alone was responsible for his victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Srinagar. “The NC never crossed 1.5 lakh votes in this parliamentary constituency in 30 to 40 years. This time I got nearly 3.80 lakh votes. The bulk of the support came from people in South Kashmir who were not associated with the NC,” he said as number of areas of South Kashmir’s Pulwama and Shopian were added to Srinagar in the delimitation exercise of 2023. He, however, said that he contested on the NC ticket and used the party's name and symbol, making his resignation necessary as he sought to distance himself from the organisation.
Mehdi, who is also a prominent shia leader, said he was reaching out to people from different walks of life, including journalists, lawyers, doctors and teachers, to build a credible political alternative.

“I am looking for people with no baggage, who have conviction and are willing to walk this path,” he said, adding that the structure and name of any new organisation would be decided later.
He said he might contest future by-elections from Srinagar constituency as an independent candidate but insisted his decision to resign was not driven by electoral ambition. “I am not bargaining with people over what I will get in return for resigning. This has nothing to do with electoral results or how people behave. It is a call of conscience and a matter of principles,” he said.

stories.headline: Odisha CM announces special package for families affected by Cyclone Arnab
stories.deck: After reviewing the prevailing flood situation in the State in the evening, CM Majhi said people in several districts, especially Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, were affected by cyclone Arnab and its aftermath of heavy rainfall
stories.bodyText:
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Sunday (November 2, 2026) announced a special package of 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 for every family affected by the recent rain and flood in the southern districts, besides damages for losses to crops and property due to Cyclone Arnab.
Also Read: Odisha short of equipment, may use explosives to rescue landslide victims
With another cyclonic storm expected to hit the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, the Chief Minister said the relief package will be reviewed again upon assessing damage after the weather system passes.
After reviewing the prevailing flood situation in the State in the evening, CM Majhi said people in several districts, especially Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, were affected by cyclone Arnab and its aftermath of heavy rainfall.
“Thousands of acres of crops and several houses have been damaged,” he told reporters and pointed out that assessment of damage was underway while the primary task was relief distribution and restoration.
Also Read: Search underway for 12 people missing in landslide-hit southern Odisha village
"I am hopeful that normalcy will return in affected areas in the next one or two days as the administration is taking all necessary measures," he said.
The Chief Minister announced that all affected families will get 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 in cash.
Small and marginal farmers, who sustained crop loss of 33% and above, will receive an agricultural input subsidy of ₹8,500 per hectare of land in rain-fed and non-irrigated areas, while ₹17,000 per hectare of land will be provided for areas under assured irrigation, he said.
Similarly, assistance for perennial crops like mango and cashew will be ₹22,500 per hectare, the Chief Minister said, adding that a minimum agricultural input subsidy of ₹2500 will be given to any affected farmer for perennial crops and ₹1000 for non-irrigated areas.
"The government will provide ₹18,000 to each affected farmer to remove sand and silt from the fields. The State will also provide 1.75 lakh mini kits to farmers for free," he added.
Under the housing sector, he said assistance of ₹1.20 lakh will be given for fully damaged houses in the plains, ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas, while ₹6,500 and ₹4,000 will be given for partially damaged pucca and kutcha houses, respectively.
CM Majhi said his government has decided to provide compensation of ₹10,000 for affected small shops, street vendors and kiosks and ₹25,000 for affected big shops and commercial establishments.
For fisherfolk, he announced assistance of ₹22,500 for boat purchase and ₹15,000 for fishing nets. Besides, financial assistance of up to 75% at a rate of ₹1.12 lakh per hectare will be distributed to affected fish farmers, CM Majhi added.
For the handicrafts and handloom sector, assistance of ₹5000 will be distributed per artisan for replacement of equipment and ₹5,000 per artisan for loss of raw material/goods in process/finished goods.

stories.headline: Cyber attacks hit Russia, Ukraine after truce ends
stories.deck: The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, ended on November 1, 2026 after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv
stories.bodyText:
Russia said its emergency warnings app came under a “massive cyberattack” on Monday (November 2, 2026), hours after Ukraine reported a hack in an apparent exchange of blows between the foes, as their longest truce came to an end.
Moscow’s emergencies ministry said hackers posted “false information” on the app, which is designed to warn the public of incoming drone attacks and other threats.
Hours earlier, Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the app.
The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday (November 1, 2026) after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv.
Moscow did not immediately say who was behind the attack on its app, while Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications SPRAVDI blamed the hack it suffered on Russia.
The rare pause in fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and which began early Tuesday, had enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as the war grinds through its fifth year.
“The ceasefire, which was in effect from October 27 to November 1, has ended,” Ukraine’s Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, said.
He called the temporary truce “an important step in our joint humanitarian efforts” with Russia.
U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume this month, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday his country would stop hitting Russian oil refineries — as U.S. counterpart Donald Trump has demanded — if Washington provided Kyiv with powerful Patriot interceptor missiles.
Raid alert app hack
Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin warned local people to be particularly vigilant when the ceasefire ended and to “respond immediately to warnings about Russian attacks”.
“The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference,” Ukraine’s air force said in a message. “There is no radiation threat.”
Air force spokesman Yuriy Ignat confirmed to AFP that the app had been hacked.
Hours later, Russia’s emergencies ministry said its teams were working to fix a “massive cyberattack” which was “enabling attackers to send false information to the public”.
‘Worse than before’
Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead and forced millions to flee their homes.
AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a “breath of fresh air”.
“We have to use this time to get things done,” said Volodymyr Omeltchenko, a 38-year-old gardener, before the truce ended.
“We’re pruning the rose bushes for winter.”
Pope Leo, who had pressed Russia for a truce in Oleshky, had said he hoped the temporary pause would “strengthen the desire for dialogue and lead to new concrete peace initiatives”.
A Ukrainian military officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, expressed concern that the fighting would be “worse than before” when it resumed.
Russian forces on the other side of the Dnipro river had taken advantage of the calm of the past few days to amass new troops, transport ammunition stocks and collect intelligence on Ukrainian positions using surveillance drones, the officer said.
Oil attacks
Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes elsewhere on Sunday.
Russia said a drone had struck an “industrial enterprise” east of Moscow overnight, with Ukrainian media reporting that Kyiv had attacked the Kstovo oil refinery.
Kyiv has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites, in what it says is fair retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
Mr. Trump has been pressing Kyiv to stop the attacks, blaming them for rising diesel costs that analysts attribute to the Iran war.
Mr. Zelenskyy said on Fox News on Sunday that he told Mr. Trump and his team: “If you want us not to attack Russia’s refineries, they have not to attack our energy system.”
“Another alternative, give us Patriot missiles,” he said.
Ukraine’s Energy Ministry reported fresh power outages across the country Sunday, including in Kyiv, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

briefs.headline: Nuclear scare, fake radiation warnings: Cyberattacks hit Russia, Ukraine alert systems
briefs.bodyText:
Ukraine and Russia have reported cyberattacks targeting their emergency alert systems, with hackers allegedly circulating fake warnings of radiation, chemical and nuclear threats, raising concerns over the disruption of public safety communications amid the ongoing war between the two countries.
Ukraine's air raid alert application was reportedly compromised on Sunday, sending false warnings about chemical and radiation threats to mobile phones across the country. Loudspeaker systems in Kyiv also broadcast similar messages, prompting the Ukrainian Air Force to warn of possible external interference.
"Attention. The Air Alert app has likely been compromised," the Air Force said on Telegram, adding that, "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!"
Ukraine's Central Intelligence Agency also reported a failure in the application and urged residents to consult alternative sources of information to verify warnings about possible air strikes.
Also Read:
'Maximum deterrence': Mojtaba Khamenei meets top generals, issues warning to US
However, the Ministry of Digital Transformation later said the nationwide alert system was functioning normally.
"The nationwide alert system is operating in normal mode. All threat signals are transmitted to regional administrations and, accordingly, to street alert systems," the ministry said in a post on X.
Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations said its mobile application had been targeted in a massive cyberattack that enabled attackers to distribute false public safety information. 
Russian authorities also reported fake warnings about nuclear strikes inside the country, with a Ukrainian espionage group reportedly suspected of involvement.
"The Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations' mobile app was subjected to a massive cyberattack, which allowed the attackers to distribute fake information to the public," the ministry said in a statement.
According to TASS, the ministry said efforts were underway to eliminate the vulnerability in the application and restore its normal functioning.
The incidents come amid continuing military operations and diplomatic efforts surrounding the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The false alerts in Ukraine were reportedly circulated shortly before the end of a localised ceasefire in the Oleshky area of Ukraine's Kherson region.
On Sunday, US First Lady Melania Trump commended Moscow and Kyiv for their cooperation during the five-day humanitarian ceasefire, which concluded on November 1. She said the arrangement had facilitated the delivery of critical humanitarian assistance and enabled the evacuation of nearly 800 people.
Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for an energy ceasefire, urging US President Donald Trump to consider the conflict's impact on global energy prices.
"If the American president thinks that this war has influence on the prices, so he can ask energy ceasefire," Zelenskyy told Fox News.

briefs.headline: 23-year-old holds 80 kg plank for 2 minutes, enters India Book of Records
briefs.deck: Pooja Smit Kumar has set a remarkable fitness record by holding a plank with an astonishing 80 kg on her back for a time of 2 minutes, 6 seconds, and 40 milliseconds. This achievement, recognized by the India Book of Records on September 9, 2026, surpasses Bijall Joshi's previous record of 75 kg for 45 seconds.
briefs.bodyText:
At a time when fitness is becoming an important part of people’s lives, a 23-year-old woman from Surat has achieved something that demands extraordinary mental as well as physical strength. Meet Patel Pooja Smit Kumar who held herself in a plank position with an additional 80 kg resting on her back for a mind-blowing 2 minutes, 6 seconds and 40 milliseconds!
Her incredible achievement has now registered her a place in the India Book of Records.
Born on July 7, 2003, Pooja's accomplishment is particularly striking because a plank, despite looking like a simple exercise, requires immense muscular strength. And adding 80 kg to the position just takes the challenge to a whole different level. Her record was confirmed on September 9, 2026, according to the India Book of Records.
What makes the achievement extraordinary?
Those who don’t know, a plank is an isometric exercise. It means the body needs to be in a fixed position while the muscles contract to maintain stability. A plank requires the person to sustain muscle engagement without switching posture.
The exercise affects the abdominal muscles, back, shoulders and other muscles responsible for stabilising the body. Maintaining a straight body alignment while supporting one's own weight is already demanding. Introducing an additional load makes the exercise considerably more challenging.
For Pooja, the challenge involved sustaining this position with 80 kg placed on her back for more than two minutes which is noteworthy.
From a 75-kg attempt to an 80-kg record
Pooja's achievement also comes against the backdrop of earlier record attempts in the same category. In January 2026, the India Book of Records recognised another woman from Surat, Bijall Joshi, for holding a plank with 75 kg on her back for 45 seconds.
The record was confirmed on January 10, 2026.
Pooja's subsequent achievement involved not only an additional five kilograms but also maintaining the position for considerably longer.
The discipline behind
Pooja Patel with her record (PC: India Book of Records) 
One reason the plank has become a familiar exercise in fitness routines is its simplicity. It requires very little equipment and can be performed in a gym or at home. But it’s not as simple as it looks.
The exercise engages several muscle groups simultaneously. The abdominal muscles help stabilise the torso, while the back and shoulder muscles contribute to maintaining the position. The hips and legs also play a role in keeping the body aligned.
At just 23, Pooja has secured recognition for an achievement that combines two important aspects of physical fitness: muscular strength and endurance. Her record also brings attention to a form of fitness that often receives less attention than conventional weightlifting or high-intensity workouts.
For many people, holding a regular plank for even a minute can be difficult. Pooja's achievement involved remaining in position for more than two minutes while carrying an additional 80 kg.
Her accomplishment is a reminder that extraordinary fitness milestones do not always involve complicated equipment or elaborate sporting arenas. Sometimes, they involve holding one position, maintaining control and pushing the limits of physical endurance.

briefs.headline: Pentagon probes whether hackers caused freezer failures at US military bases
briefs.deck: In August, several US military bases experienced food spoilage due to freezer failures, potentially caused by a cyberattack. Investigators, including US Cyber Command, have not confirmed the technical cause or identified any suspects. French authorities are being coordinated with as similar incidents affected supermarkets in France earlier this month. The Food and Agriculture Information Sharing…
briefs.bodyText:
The Pentagon is investigating whether a cyberattack triggered a series of commercial freezer failures that spoiled food across multiple US military bases in August, according to a US official familiar with the matter. The disruptions hit approximately six commissaries -- the on-base grocery stores serving service members and their families -- the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing probe. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, base officials discovered that a walk-in freezer had unexpectedly shifted into defrost mode, heating its inventory and ruining the stored provisions.
The US Cyber Command and Defense Department law enforcement agencies are leading the inquiry. Investigators have not publicly identified any suspects or formally confirmed the technical root cause behind the equipment failures. Reuters first reported Thursday that investigators were treating the incidents as a possible hack. It’s unclear who might be responsible or whether investigators have conclusively determined what caused the failures.
The US investigators are also coordinating with French authorities. 
Earlier this month, hackers manipulated temperature controls on commercial cooling systems across more than 350 locations in France, forcing widespread inventory disposal at local supermarkets.
What happened in France
In early October, hackers targeted hundreds of French supermarkets in a cyberattack that reportedly caused refrigerators and freezers to overheat, spoiling food and sparking fires.
Fridges at French supermarket chains Carrefour, Monoprix, the Les Mousquetaires-owned Intermarche, and Cooperative U, among others, all saw fridges heat up to as much as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight. The incident highlights growing vulnerabilities in operational technology—the internet-connected industrial control systems that regulate everyday supply chain infrastructure. While critical infrastructure discussions often center on power grids and water treatment facilities, cybersecurity analysts warn that food storage systems frequently rely on remote-access controls protected by weak defenses.
Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center's warning
The Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC), an industry threat-intelligence group, has repeatedly warned that internet-accessible industrial controls present an easy target for malicious actors. Because the food sector cannot tolerate extended downtime without severe financial and logistical losses, facilities remain prime targets for extortion and ransomware campaigns. A 2021 Department of Homeland Security assessment similarly warned that cyber-induced refrigeration failures posed direct risks to national food distribution networks.
The August commissary failures were first noted publicly by the Signal and Silence blog, followed by reporting from Stars and Stripes on the military's involvement and The Telegraph on international coordination with France. 
In Congress, the incidents have renewed momentum around supply chain security. Lawmakers reintroduced the bipartisan Farm and Food Cybersecurity Act in 2025, aiming to bolster crisis response protocols and federal threat-sharing mechanisms across the nation’s agricultural and distribution pipelines.

briefs.headline: How are tropical cyclones named?
briefs.deck: Tropical cyclones are the second-most dangerous natural hazards, after earthquakes
briefs.bodyText:
Cyclone 'Murasu' has intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal on November 2, 2026.
The IMD, or India Meteorological Department, says that the system may continue to move northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast, near Ongole, as a Severe Cyclonic Storm, with wind speeds expected to be between 100 to 110 kmph, gusting 120 kmph.
Cyclone Murasu comes days after Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh
Chennai and Tiruvallur District Collectors have announced that schools and colleges in the districts will be closed on Monday (November 2, 2026) due to heavy rains. An orange alert was announced in six Telangana districts and a yellow alert in five districts in Telangana for Monday.
What are tropical cyclones?
A tropical cyclone is a rapidly rotating storm that begins over a tropical ocean and can vary in speed, size, and intensity. They are also called hurricanes or typhoons, depending on the region.
Tropical cyclones are the second-most dangerous natural hazards, after earthquakes, according to the World Meteorological Organisation.
How are cyclones named?
The WMO elaborates that the process of determining names for tropical cyclones is conducted by the relevant tropical cyclone regional body at its annual or biennial session.
There are five tropical cyclone regional bodies, which are:
- WMO Typhoon Committee
- WMO Panel on Tropical Cyclones
- Regional Association I Tropical Cyclone Committee
- Regional Association IV Hurricane Committee
- Regional Association V Tropical Cyclone Committee
These bodies establish pre-designated lists of names, the procedures for which can vary, with some regions using alphabetical order and others using the alphabetical order of country names. No tropical cyclone is named after an individual.
Factors that are considered while selecting a new name:
- Short in character length for ease of use in communication.
- Easy to pronounce
- Appropriate significance in different languages
- Uniqueness- same names cannot be used in other regions.
The WMO adds that the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) New Delhi Tropical Cyclone Centre is responsible for naming the tropical cyclones that have formed over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea when they have reached the relevant intensity.
Cyclones that form in the Northern Indian Ocean are named in a cyclical fashion by thirteen countries — Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.
How are tropical cyclones classified?
The classification of a tropical cyclone depends on its maximum sustained wind speed. They are designated as follows:
1. Tropical depression is when the maximum sustained windspeed is less than 63 km/hour.
2.Tropical storm is when the maximum sustained wind speed is more than 63 km/hour. It is then also given a name.
3. Hurricane, typhoon, tropical cyclone, very severe cyclonic storm, depending on the basin, when the maximum sustained wind speed exceeds 116 km/hour.

briefs.headline: Jet crash in Florida: All nine people aboard killed, says Transportation Secretary
briefs.deck: The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration
briefs.bodyText:
All nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Duffy said the Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation into the cause.
The Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway, creating a giant fiery crater in the pavement.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
“This is definitely a tragedy,” he said.
He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD.
Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.
The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.
A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.

briefs.headline: Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' phone call
briefs.deck: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's…
briefs.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a telephone conversation on Saturday to discuss Washington's negotiations with Iran and the possibility of resuming military operations, with Netanyahu pressing for fresh strikes after Tuesday's US midterm elections, according to a report by Axios.
The call came amid differences over the approach towards Tehran, with the Israeli prime minister urging immediate military action after the elections, while Trump wants to allow diplomatic efforts to continue for now, Axios reported, citing one Israeli and one US source.
An Israeli source described the conversation as "tough", while a US source called it "direct".
However, Trump told reporters in Iowa on Sunday that he had a "very good talk" with Netanyahu and confirmed that Iran was among the subjects discussed, without giving further details.
The White House and the Israeli prime minister's office declined to comment on the call.
Also Read: 
'They'll become garbage': Trump says he'll become 'Mr. Veto'if Democrats win midterms
Trump keeps diplomatic and military options open
Trump is pursuing parallel diplomatic and military approaches, seeking an agreement that could restart peace talks with Iran while keeping preparations underway for a possible return to major combat operations after the midterm elections.
Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Trump said negotiations with Iran were "going fine" and that he was not "in much of a hurry". 
He also said Tehran wanted a deal but questioned its reliability.
"They make a deal and then they back out," Trump said.
At the same time, the US president indicated that Washington still needed to address one or two nuclear sites in Iran. Referring to the suspected underground facility at Pickaxe Mountain, he said, "We can do that in 10 minutes. We have that planned. You can look at Pickaxe Mountain. We need to take care of that. We can do that very quickly."
The US was keeping the possibility of renewed military action open even as it pursued negotiations.
Vance's outreach and Qatar's mediation
The diplomatic engagement has included a letter sent last week by US Vice President JD Vance to Iran's national security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, concerning the possibility of restarting negotiations. It was the highest-level US outreach to Tehran in several months.
Meanwhile, Qatari mediators met Iranian officials on Sunday for the third consecutive day in an effort to reach an agreement that would allow direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran to resume.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said no agreement had been reached so far and that progress depended on the US responding to questions raised by Tehran.
"We are making every effort in this regard and hope that the other side will demonstrate enough rationality to choose diplomacy over other paths," Araghchi said.
In an interview shared on his Telegram channel, Araghchi said consultations with mediators were continuing and that the final outcome depended on the answers provided by Washington to Iran's questions.
He said Iran remained prepared for both defence and diplomacy, depending on the US response. Araghchi had also said on Saturday that Iranian negotiators were in Qatar discussing a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington met several conditions.
He stressed that no direct talks were taking place between Iran and the US, AP reported.
The latest diplomatic efforts come as the two sides explore the possibility of restarting negotiations while the prospect of renewed military operations remains under discussion.

briefs.headline: Brazil elections | Historic win, humongous challenges
briefs.deck: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme
briefs.bodyText:
At the end of the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva looked like a leader on his way out after a record third term. He trailed Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2% to 47%, hurt by an abstention rate of 21%, the highest since 1998, as many of his supporters stayed home.
In the three weeks that followed, Mr. Lula managed a remarkable turnaround, helped by several factors. First, the day after the first round, thousands of students from the Fluminense Federal University marched through the streets of Niteroi to stand against Bolsonarism. Days later, thousands more young people occupied Candelaria Square in Rio de Janeiro. Similar student, youth and workers’ marches soon spread across urban Brazil. The protesters gathered without party banners, united less by support for Mr. Lula than by opposition to Bolsonarism, a far-right movement opposed to institutions, supportive of high-handed actions against crime and eager to curtail civil liberties. The newspaper O Globo described the marches as the Left’s return to the streets after more than a decade of absence.

stories.headline: ‘Husband Husband’ to ‘????’ and ‘XXX’: After SIR, Bengaluru’s electoral rolls riddled with errors
stories.deck: In some polling stations, large clusters of consecutive entries have names and their relatives’ details replaced by jumbled letters and symbols, leaving several entries unrecognisable.
stories.bodyText:
From names appearing as “XXX” or “??????K” to missing relatives’ names and entries containing single letters, email IDs or even “...”, entries in Bengaluru’s final electoral rolls are riddled with errors. The Hindu found discrepancies in at least 1,000 entries here alone.
In some polling parts, voters listed one after another (consecutive serial numbers) have had their names and their relatives’ names replaced by jumbled letters, making it impossible to identify them from the entries in the voter rolls.
Diacritical entries
In Dasarahalli Assembly constituency, which has 425 electors, an unusually large number of consecutive entries in polling part No. 324 carry garbled names. The electors’ names and relatives’ names at serial numbers 4 to 7, 143 to 150, 152 to 157, 300 to 302, 306 to 313, 327 to 330, and 336 to 340 appeared as strings of unfamiliar characters.
Serial number 327, for example, listed the elector’s name as “µ¢µÌèÌ” and the relative’s name as “Ï¢µÈèÈ”. This combination was seen across all mentioned serial numbers.
Errors were also found in the names of relatives. This column was left blank or contained only a single letter in several entries in the final rolls. Others listed “NA”, “None”, while some had the relationship itself — such as “Husband”, “Wife” or “Mother”, entered in place of the relative’s name.
In Dasarahalli (polling part No. 7), an elector named Kavitha had her name split between English and Kannada even in the English version of the roll, while the relative’s name was listed as “Husband Husband”. In Chamarajpet, an elector, Abdul Salam, had “Wife” entered as the relative’s name. In Mahadevapura, some entries listed only a single letter, such as “S” or “B”, as the relative’s name.
Email IDs and numbers
There were also entries containing details that appeared to have no connection with the fields in which they were recorded, including dates and e-mail addresses.
In Yelahanka Assembly constituency, in polling part No. 332, an elector’s relative’s name was listed as “rakshithagowda1430@gmail.comgowda”. In another entry in the BBMP South district, the relative’s name appeared as “Syed Apsar KZW1566785”. A 50-year-old man’s name, meanwhile, was listed as “Channapa Gowda Patil 01/06/1974”, while a 44-year-old female was listed as “??????K”.
The Hindu contacted AEROs and BLO supervisors, who said they were unaware of the cases and would look into them.
A polling official, however, attributed the problem to an error during transliteration. The official said some fonts used special codes to display Kannada letters. “If the computer could not recognise the font used when the file was converted, the letters could appear as unrelated symbols,” he said.
BLOs, too, attributed the errors to software glitches. At least three BLOs said they had encountered similar problems and had informed their supervisors about them. “Only a few people reached out regarding this after the final rolls, and we have told them to fill Form 8 (seeking correction). We were aware of such errors as the software kept showing these glitches, but we were told that after the final upload, the system would fix them,” they said.
The Hindu also spoke to many such voters whose names or other details appeared incorrectly in the rolls to find out what information they had submitted. In most of the cases, the electors said they had provided the correct details. Some said they had noticed the errors but assumed they were temporary glitches, as the names were illegible. They said they realised that their details had appeared incorrectly only later, when they identified their entries by their house numbers.

stories.headline: Over Rs 960cr scam? 127 plots sold, then mortgaged to scam-hit bank in Bengaluru
stories.deck: Fresh allegations of fraud have emerged related to Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha involving mortgaged properties. Properties with ongoing financial disputes had previously been sold to unsuspecting buyers, exposing a troubling issue. The bank lacks accurate data on these properties, complicating efforts to determine ownership and value. An association representing affected…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: More than five years after Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha in south Bengaluru went bust leaving hundreds of depositors in dire straits, fresh allegations of fraud have come to light, with properties already sold to unsuspecting buyers having been mortgaged with the bank.
In one case, the outstanding amount against the mortgaged property is Rs 961 crore even though the value of the collateral is not known.
According to officials, the bank does not have accurate information about the value of these properties, which are spread across the city and cover 45 to 50 acres. The farthest property mortgaged to the bank is in Chintamani, Kolar.
Documents in possession of 
TOI show a Bangalore Development Authority-approved Sri Shankara Layout in Kambipura village, Kengeri hobli of Bengaluru, was mortgaged along with 127 plots that had already been sold to innocent individuals.
The layout has a registered residents’ welfare association, whose members say they learnt of the mortgage only recently.
On July 16, 2026, the layout owners’ welfare association wrote a letter to the administrator of Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha and said that between 2011 and 2015, there was an absolute sale deed executed by the developers of the layout with each of the 127 individuals.
The letter acknowledged as received by the bank administrator said two mortgage deeds registered and dated Oct 31, 2019, and two rectification deeds of Nov 28, 2019… along with residential plots formed on them in entirety, were shown as collateral security to your bank which was then represented by then chief advisor M Vasudev Maiya to obtain huge amounts of loans from the bank.
The association asked how the bank could have accepted the plots as collateral when absolute sale deeds had already been executed in the buyers’ favour.
It claimed the case involved criminal breach of trust by the developers, allegedly in connivance with bank officials at the time. The association urged the bank administrator not to initiate any proceedings or take steps which may damage or dent their interest, rights and stake over the physical possession of their respective residential plots.
A notice issued by the bank to the layout’s developers in Jan 2026 said loans totalling Rs 739 crore and 87 lakh had been raised by mortgaging the property to various persons. With interest, the outstanding amount was Rs 961 crore.
Bank officials, on condition of anonymity, told 
TOI that in as many as 10 to 15 cases of property mortgages, the then bank officials had attached “unsecured” loans to evade audit lacunae.
“These accounts are being termed ‘rollover accounts’, wherein unsecured loans were being attached to mortgaged properties. While the actual loan recipient would have received Rs 10 to Rs 12 crore, the rest of the loan amount was given out to other people,” said one senior bank official.
In the case of Shankara Layout developers, 23 people apart from the original loan recipients were given money. Beneficiaries of these loans include individuals and companies.
On Shankara Layout, bank officials said they would take a factual position on whether the Sri Shankara Layout plots were sold before or after the land was mortgaged in 2019. “Properties sold prior to the mortgaged dates cannot be included in the recovery process,” said officials, adding that the plot owners were sending their documents individually to the bank.

stories.headline: Govt mulls official status for Kannada flag, plans Belagavi debate
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Sunday said Karnataka govt was considering granting official recognition to the red-and-yellow Kannada flag as the state’s flag without affecting the dignity of the Tricolour.
“The yellow-and-red flag has become an integral symbol of the state’s identity. We’ll discuss the matter and explore legal options in the upcoming Belagavi legislative session,” the CM said at the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations here.
He said the state had earlier passed a cabinet resolution and submitted a proposal to the Centre, but approval was awaited.
This is not the first time the Congress govt has attempted to secure official status for the Kannada flag. In 2018, the Siddaramaiah-led govt proposed a redesigned state flag and sought recognition for it. Asked whether govt would consider the new design, Shivakumar said, “The flag we are proposing is the plain yellow-and-red that is widely used across Karnataka.”
Shivakumar said the govt was considering making the hoisting of Kannada flag mandatory at govt offices and institutions receiving govt support. The announcement comes amid renewed discussions on Kannada identity and language promotion.
A long-pending demand for extending grant-in-aid benefits to Kannada-medium aided schools established after 1995 found mention at the celebrations. Responding to school education minister Madhu Bangarappa’s request in this regard, the CM said the govt would soon call representatives of Kannada-aided schools and discuss the matter with the finance department on grants.
Such recognition primarily covers teacher salary expenditure, with sanctioned teaching posts coming under govt funding.
Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools in Karnataka (KAMS) general secretary D Shashi Kumar said the demand has been pending for several years. “These are Kannada-medium schools that have continued to function without grant support,” he said.
Gram Anubhava launched: The CM launched Gram Anubhava, which aims to expose urban school students to rural life, covering students of Classes 8, 9 and 11.
50% off on Kannada books in Nov: Kuvempu Bhasha Bharathi Pradhikara has announced a 50% discount from Nov 1 to 30 on all its publications as part of Rajyotsava celebrations.

stories.headline: Karnataka turns to U.K. roadshows to revive declining NRI tourist footfall
stories.bodyText:
Amid a decline in the number of Non-Resident Indian (NRI) tourists visiting Karnataka, the State Tourism Department is participating in the World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026 roadshow, scheduled to be held from November 2 to 6.
The WTM London 2026 is a premier global meeting place for travel industry and professionals of hospitality industry, stakeholders and others to exhibit tourist places of their respective countries, States and attend various sessions that reflect on improving tourism.
Around 180 countries participate in the event with more than 4,000 exhibitors and over 40,000 participants.
A senior official from the Tourism Department, said, “For the first time, these road shows and sessions are being held in Manchester and Birmingham. Earlier, a lot of NRI tourists came to Karnataka for tourism. Post the COVID pandemic, the number of tourists visiting places have reduced to more than 50%. We want to revive this footfall through our roadshow. The reason is they are visiting tourist places like Maldives, Bali, Abu Dhabi and other countries in the Middle East.”
The official said, “In order to attract them back to Karnataka and also other foreign tourists especially those from London, Germany, the U.S., Australia, we are holding these road shows to promote the State tourism.”
According to the officials, around nine people are selected to participate in the event to promote the State tourism. “They will put up posters, audio-visual displays of tourist places in Karnataka on an LED screen. They will also explain the importance of these places to the participants, accomodation facilities available, ease of travel and other options,” the official said.
Through this road show, the officials are hoping that by the end of this year or the beginning of next year of tourism season, the department hopes to attract more NRIs to the world famous places in the State.

briefs.headline: After milk-curd, Karnataka bus fares will go up on November 5

The minister cited rising diesel prices and significant losses for state transport corporations as reasons for this adjustment. Addressing concerns over fare comparisons with other states, he mentioned a meeting on November 4 to…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: 
Karnataka
 transport minister Byrathi Suresh on Sunday confirmed that the proposed bus fare hike by Karnataka’s state-run transport corporations would come into effect on Nov 5, adding to the financial burden on commuters just five days after the state govt increased milk prices.
Suresh, who made the announcement in Chikkaballapur, said the quantum of hike will be decided at a meeting on Nov 4.
He alleged that the BJP-led central govt had increased diesel prices five times in the past year, resulting in an annual loss of Rs 2,000 crore for the four state-run transport corporations. Their cumulative losses have already reached Rs 9,000 crore, he said.
The issue was discussed at a recent cabinet meeting, which entrusted CM 
DK Shivakumar
 and the transport department with the responsibility of deciding on the fare revision, Suresh said.
Responding to criticism by Chikkaballapur MP K Sudhakar over the proposed hike, Suresh said bus fares in Karnataka were lower than those in other states.
Sudhakar should compare fares in BJP-ruled states instead of making statements without considering the facts, Suresh said, questioning whether the loss-making transport corporations should be shut down rather than being allowed to recover financially.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express flagged off by Railway Minister
briefs.deck: The overnight service will connect Bengaluru with Mumbai via Anantapur, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Pune, improving connectivity across three States
briefs.bodyText:
Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Sunday (November 1) flagged off the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express, introducing a new overnight rail service connecting two of the country’s major economic centres.
The new service will connect Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal (SMVT), Bengaluru, with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai, passing through important stations in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra.
Highlighting the significance of the service, Mr. Vaishnaw said that the train would connect Bengaluru, India’s IT and start-up capital, with Mumbai, the country’s financial capital. It is expected to benefit professionals, entrepreneurs, students, traders, business travellers and tourists.
Six-day service across three States
The train will run through Anantapur and Guntakal in Andhra Pradesh; Raichur, Yadgir, Wadi and Kalaburagi in Karnataka; and Solapur, Pune and Kalyan in Maharashtra.
The service is expected to improve overnight connectivity, particularly for passengers from North Karnataka, by providing access to a modern sleeper train service, according to railway officials.
According to the announced schedule, the train will depart SMVT Bengaluru at 7.45 p.m. and reach CSMT Mumbai at 11.55 a.m. the following day. In the return direction, it will leave Mumbai at 8.10 p.m. and arrive in Bengaluru at noon the next day.
The service will operate six days a week, except Mondays from Bengaluru and Tuesdays from Mumbai. The introduction of the Bengaluru-Mumbai service follows the launch of Vande Bharat Sleeper services on the Howrah-Guwahati corridor in January 2026 and the flagging off of the Varanasi-New Delhi service on Saturday (October 31).
Bengaluru-Hubballi Vande Bharat Sleeper service
Meanwhile, Mr. Vaishnaw also announced plans to introduce another Vande Bharat Sleeper service from Bengaluru towards the Hubballi region, extending towards Pune and Mumbai. The proposed service is expected to strengthen connectivity with north Karnataka.
He further said that Vande Bharat services between Bengaluru and Mangaluru are expected to commence within the next few weeks, subject to the completion of electrification and successful testing on the route. The service is expected to improve rail connectivity between Bengaluru and coastal Karnataka.
Highlighting other railway infrastructure developments, the Union Minister highlighted the expansion of high-speed rail connectivity in Karnataka and the development of new railway corridors to strengthen regional connectivity and promote economic integration. Highlighting the expected reduction in travel time, he stated that the Bengaluru-Chennai journey would take just 73 minutes, while Bengaluru-Hyderabad connectivity would be covered in approximately two hours and 10 minutes.

briefs.headline: Tumakuru police arrest Madhya Pradesh-based Dhar gang member, recover valuables worth ₹23 lakh
briefs.deck: The theft took place on September 17, 2026, when a KSRTC Airavat bus was stopped near a hotel within the limits of the Kallambella police station for breakfast at around 7 am.
briefs.bodyText:
The Tumakuru district police have arrested a suspected member of the notorious inter-State Dhar gang from Madhya Pradesh and recovered diamond, gold and silver ornaments worth approximately ₹23 lakh in connection with a theft aboard a Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) Airavat bus in Sira taluk.
The theft took place on September 17, 2026, when a KSRTC Airavat bus was stopped near a hotel within the limits of the Kallambella police station for breakfast at around 7 am. Taking advantage of the halt, the accused allegedly entered the bus and decamped with a briefcase containing the ornaments.
The stolen valuables were estimated to be worth ₹30.62 lakh. Based on a complaint filed by B.S. Sridhar, a resident of Davangere Town, the Kallambella police registered a case and launched an investigation
A special team was formed under the guidance of Tumakuru Superintendent of Police Ashok K.V.
The team travelled to Kherwa village in Manawar taluk of Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, on October 24 and arrested Sefalikhan alias Gulresha Khan, son of Guljar Khan, on October 28, according to police officials.
The police recovered a diamond necklace set, two pairs of gold earrings weighing approximately 12 gm and four gm, respectively, and a silver Lakshmi idol weighing around 36 gm. The recovered valuables are worth approximately ₹23 lakh.

The Bengaluru city corporations on Sunday formally launched the “Ward One” initiative, which was taken up based on the directions of Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda, to address micro-level issues at the ward level.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru 5-star hotel tragedy: CCTV footage suggests electrical fault near pool entrance
briefs.deck: Recent CCTV footage suggests that a malfunctioning electrical system near the pool's entrance might have caused a tragic incident at the Conrad Hotel. On October 30, two foreign nationals, Alexander Maximilian Theiss and Juraj Horvat, lost their lives due to electrocution while swimming. Injuries were also reported for Mathew Desantis and Rahul Tiwari.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: CCTV footage examined by Halasuru police investigating the deaths of two foreign nationals at Conrad Hotel’s swimming pool suggests that the suspected electrical fault may have originated near the entrance railings and steps, where LED lights are installed.
The footage offers a sequence of events leading up to the Oct 30 incident, in which German national Alexander Maximilian Theiss, 57, a Lufthansa crew member, and Slovak national Juraj Horvat, 45, a project manager with IBM, died of electrocution. Police suspect that power from the lighting system or its wiring may have leaked into the pool.
TOI
 had reported Sunday under the headline, “Bigger tragedy averted? Current confined to 5m radius, probe finds.”
A senior officer said he inspected the spot and examined the CCTV footage, which shows Theiss jumping into the pool from the opposite side and swimming towards the entrance. After covering about half the distance, he stopped briefly and then continued swimming. Horvat, meanwhile, collapsed in the water shortly after entering the pool, between 5.10pm and 5.15pm.
The two others injured were American tourist Mathew Desantis, 41, and hotel employee Rahul Tiwari, 28. 
According to the officer, Desantis, who was already in the pool, felt an electric current while swimming but managed to get out and alert the hotel staff.
Tiwari, who rushed to rescue the two men, also suffered an electric shock and is undergoing treatment. Desantis has since been discharged.
Electrical inspectors, Bescom officials and police visited the pool Saturday and collected evidence. “We are waiting for reports from experts, file a final report before the court and take action against the hotel management,” the officer said.
Hotel staff get summons
Police have begun compiling a list of hotel employees who were on duty on Oct 30. They have collected details of staff responsible for electrical maintenance, pool operations and other related work, and issued summons to some of them.
“Based on the CCTV footage, there is no foul play in the deaths of the two men,” the officer said.
T
he body of Theiss was handed over to the German consulate general after the post-mortem Sunday. Consulate officials, representatives of the airline and others were present during the procedure.
Horvat’s wife, Silvia Hotuatova, who had filed a complaint in the case, returned to Slovakia Saturday night. She had stayed at the hotel after returning from the hospital and asked officials to send her husband’s body after completing the required formalities.
“We are in contact with the Slovakian consulate. The post-mortem will be conducted after they give their consent, and the body will be handed over thereafter,” the officer said.

briefs.headline: Hotel Conrad tragedy in Bengaluru: Swimming association to issue guidelines on pool safety
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Following the death of two foreign nationals in a suspected electrocution at Conrad hotel’s swimming pool, Karnataka Swimming Association (KSA) plans to issue a comprehensive safety advisory to swimming clubs, educational institutions, hotels and other pool operators across the state.
The association intends to cover electrical safety, proper earthing, periodic inspection of electrical installations, underwater lighting, filtration and pumping systems, availability of trained lifeguards, and emergency response arrangements. It will also emphasise first-aid facilities, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), regular safety audits, and proper maintenance records.
KSA president and former IGP Gopal Hosur told 
TOI
 that the association was keen to work with the state govt and the departments concerned to strengthen the implementation of safety norms. “Karnataka Swimming Association can, at best, issue a comprehensive advisory on swimming pool safety. Safety cannot be treated as a one-time certification. It has to be a continuous process,” he said.
Hosur proposed a joint initiative involving the sports department, municipal authorities, the electrical inspectorate, fire and emergency services, and other relevant agencies. Measures could include a survey and registration of swimming pools across Karnataka, mandatory periodic safety inspections and certification, and a uniform safety checklist for public and commercial pools.
The association could also provide technical expertise in framing guidelines, conducting awareness programmes, and training personnel. However, statutory enforcement would have to rest with the appropriate govt authorities, he said.
On whether the Conrad incident could have been prevented, Hosur said it would be premature to arrive at a conclusion before the technical investigation is completed. Authorities must establish the source of the suspected electrical leakage and determine whether there were deficiencies in installation, earthing, maintenance or safety systems.
“Swimming pools are particularly sensitive environments where water and electricity can create a potentially fatal combination. Proper electrical design, effective earthing, functioning earth-leakage protection devices, periodic inspection by qualified professionals and strict maintenance protocols are essential safeguards,” he said, adding that lifeguard presence and emergency preparedness were equally important but could not substitute for electrical safety.

briefs.headline: Mahatma Gandhi play row: Ink smeared on former Rangayana director’s face in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A theatrical performance titled 
The Truth Behind Freedom Fighter Mahatma Gandhi’s Assassination
 sparked a controversy at Suchitra Cinema and Cultural Academy in Banashankari after former Mysuru Rangayana director Addanda Cariappa allegedly had ink smeared on his face during a confrontation with Congress workers.
Two counter-complaints were filed at Banashankari police station.
Organised by Kodagu Rangabhoomi Trust and directed by Cariappa, the play came under fire from Congress workers and members of various organisations over alleged objectionable remarks about Mahatma Gandhi.
In a complaint, a Congress worker alleged the play spread misinformation about Gandhi’s assassination and portrayed him as anti-national. The protesters also accused Cariappa of blaming Gandhi and Congress for the Partition of India.
Protesters entered the academy and confronted the organisers. A heated exchange followed, during which Cariappa was allegedly manhandled. The complainants also alleged that tickets for the play had been sold on the black market in Mysuru and that those who questioned the alleged irregularities were verbally abused. 
They sought action against Cariappa and the performers.
In his counter-complaint, Cariappa alleged the protesters disrupted the performance, assaulted him and threatened to kill him. He maintained that the play was based on references from books.
Banashankari police registered both complaints as non-cognisable reports (NCRs).
At 10pm, around 15 Congress workers attempted to enter the police commissioner’s office on Infantry Road. Police turned them away, assuring them that necessary action would be taken.

briefs.headline: A saree’s journey from Paris to Molakalmuru revives forgotten weaving technique at Bengaluru exhibition
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A saree displayed in a Paris museum, catalogued simply as being from south India, caught the eye of a textile revivalist and set in motion an effort to revive a forgotten weaving technique in Karnataka.
When Lavina Baldota noticed the saree, she felt it had a connection with Molakalmuru. “The language of the weave had a remarkable similarity with the region’s textile tradition,” she said, recounting the story at the inauguration of Pampa – Textiles of Karnataka at National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) Sunday.
Lavina and her team tracked down Manjunath DS, a weaver whose family has practised the craft at Molakalmuru in Chitradurga district for generations. After studying the saree’s weave, they found that it required a Jala loom, a technique once practised in the region but which gradually disappeared. Manjunath took up the challenge, learnt the technique and set up a loom to recreate the saree. While the ikkat was tie-dyed in Telangana, the saree was eventually woven in Molakalmuru.
For Manjunath, the exercise was also an opportunity to revive a tradition practised by his ancestors. 
He said the technique had gradually faded because it required more time and manpower, making it difficult to sustain.
Lavina said the idea for Pampa began with a question from fellow curator Mayank Mansingh Kaul about whether there was a book on Karnataka’s textile traditions. The absence of a comprehensive account of the state’s diverse textile traditions prompted a search that turned into a journey of discovery. The curatorial team, which also included Nupur Saxena, documented traditions and met weavers and communities across the state.
Organised by Abheraj Baldota Foundation to mark its 50th anniversary, Pampa is presented in collaboration with the Union ministry of culture and NGMA Bengaluru. It brings together more than 150 textiles, artworks and installations, tracing Karnataka’s handmade and hand-patterned textile traditions from the 18th century to the present.
Union minister for culture and tourism 
Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
 described textiles as “living archives of our civilisational evolution and development”.
The inauguration was attended by state chief secretary Shalini Rajneesh, NGMA director-general Sanjeev Kishor Gautam, NGMA Bengaluru director Priyanka Mary Francis and Baldota Group chairman Narendra Kumar Baldota.
First showcased at Hampi in March 2025, the exhibition seeks to highlight the cultural, social and economic significance of Karnataka’s textile traditions through recurring showcases. It will remain open to the public at NGMA Bengaluru until Dec 15.

stories.headline: $3.64 billion pulled from world's largest crypto exchange Binance after $6.3 billion heist
stories.deck: Customers withdrew substantial amounts from Binance following a significant security breach that resulted in a major cryptocurrency theft. Despite initial panic, Binance reassured users and resumed withdrawal services for several cryptocurrencies. The exchange replaced nearly all stolen assets, utilizing its own funds for the recovery. Meanwhile, the broader cryptocurrency market showed signs of…
stories.bodyText:
Customers withdrew $3.64 billion from Binance after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange last week, triggering an initial rush of withdrawals as users moved to protect their assets. Binance said the outflows were now stabilising as it resumed services following the security breach.
The withdrawals accounted for around 2.1 per cent of Binance's total assets. The exchange, which had $171 billion in assets under management as of October 28, said deposit volumes had remained "substantial" despite the initial spike in withdrawals.
"(That) puts the withdrawals in the range of a precautionary reaction rather than any sort of capital flight," Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, said, as quoted by Reuters.
The pace of withdrawals is being closely watched as an early indicator of whether customers continue to trust the platform following one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record.
Binance has sought to reassure users that the financial damage from the breach would not be passed on to them. The company said it had replaced around 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds, spending approximately $6 billion to buy replacement tokens. 
The remaining 5 per cent comprises less liquid cryptocurrencies that could take longer to source in the required quantities.
The exchange resumed withdrawals in phases on Sunday, initially allowing transactions involving 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Dogecoin and some stablecoins such as USDT and USDC. Binance said it was prioritising tokens based on user demand over the past week.
"We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand," the exchange said in a post on X, adding, "Rest assured that market conditions are stable."
However, data from crypto analytics platform DefiLlama showed higher outflows of $5.81 billion, up from the $4.36 billion it had reported earlier. Binance disputed the figures, saying they did not account for certain deposits into its new hot wallet.
"This figure does not contain the flows we have deposited to our own new hot wallet, so they are not accurate. Our last update on X is closest to accurate," a Binance spokesperson said.
The broader cryptocurrency market also showed signs of recovering after the initial shock. Bitcoin, which touched a six-week low on Friday, traded above $78,000 on Monday, while Ether recovered to around $2,287 after hitting a two-month low.
Meanwhile, the combined market capitalisation of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, declined by around $1.2 billion since Friday, according to CoinMarketCap.
Binance has said it will bear the financial cost of the breach, setting aside approximately $6.34 billion from its corporate treasury, Futures Insurance Fund and Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to cover the losses.

stories.headline: Oil prices today: Crude falls over 1% as Iran-Qatar talks raise hopes of diplomacy
stories.deck: Oil prices dropped over 1% following ongoing talks between Iranian and Qatari officials aimed at reducing conflict. Brent crude futures fell to $111.84, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell to $102.56. The drop in prices followed a strong increase seen last week before the US midterm elections. Opec+ has kept production targets unchanged due to ongoing disruptions. Market observers remain…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices fell more than 1% on Monday as Iranian and Qatari officials held talks for a third consecutive day aimed at securing an agreement to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, easing some immediate concerns over supply disruptions.
Brent crude futures declined $1.59, or 1.40%, to $111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT.
US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell $1.56, or 1.50%, to $102.56 a barrel, according to Reuters.
The decline followed a strong rise last week, with Brent ending October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.
Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, said the fall reflected a technical correction after last week's gains, alongside hopes of progress in diplomatic efforts.
"Oil is seeing a technical pullback this morning after last week’s strong gains," Waterer said, as quoted by Reuters.
"Lingering hopes of some form of diplomatic progress, combined with the absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend, have taken some of the immediate heat out of prices for now."
However, he cautioned that the market remained alert to the possibility of stronger rhetoric over Iran, which could push Brent crude towards $120 a barrel after the midterm elections.
Iran-Qatar talks and Strait of Hormuz disruptions
The latest price movement came as Iranian and Qatari officials continued consultations aimed at facilitating an agreement to restart direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" discussions was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators. He added that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy".
The diplomatic efforts are taking place against the backdrop of attacks on oil tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz, which have pushed up global energy and shipping costs.
The waterway is a key route for global oil shipments, and disruptions to tanker movements have remained a concern for energy markets during the conflict.
Opec+ keeps December output targets unchanged
Meanwhile, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, a grouping known as Opec+, kept their December production targets unchanged on Sunday.
The decision was in line with market expectations and indicated that the group would not make further policy adjustments until next year, as it continues to face export disruptions linked to the Iran war.
Separately, Saudi Arabia increased its crude oil exports in October compared with September, despite attacks by Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthi forces on its energy infrastructure, Reuters reported, citing two of three ship-tracking companies.
The developments in the Gulf, the outcome of diplomatic efforts involving Iran and Qatar, and the possibility of renewed military escalation after the US midterm elections remain key factors for oil markets.

stories.headline: VBJ to look at going public in 3 to 4 years
stories.bodyText:
Chennai-based VBJ (Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers) plans to look at going public in three to four years.
VBJ Managing Directors Amarendran Vummidi and Jithendra Vummidi told The Hindu on Sunday that the company is looking at a topline of ₹3,000 crore during the 2026-2027 financial year and plans to achieve ₹5,000 annual revenue in a couple of years. “We should be able to achieve ₹10,000 crore turnover in three years. We will look at IPO then,” said Mr. Amarendran Vummidi.
The growth in revenue will come from the brand expanding its footprint and with the increasing value of gold.
VBJ opened a 21,000 sq.ft outlet in Coimbatore on Sunday at a total investment of ₹900 crore (land, building, and stock) and will open outlets in Tiruchi, Hyderabad, and T-Nagar by the end of the current fiscal. It will invest ₹350 crore each in Chrompet, T-Nagar, and Tiruchi, they added. With one outlet in Texas, another one is planned in California in January.
“Today, every brand is expanding its footprint. Geographically, we need to be close to the customers. The market is there for everyone to expand. Our brand has patronage and demand for new stores. With the products, we do not want to lose focus on new designs,” added Mr. Jithendra Vummidi on opening of new stores.
VBJ is also developing technology in house to reach out to young customers with digi gold.

stories.headline: Coal India’s production increases 19% as mining recovers after monsoon slump

stories.bodyText:
Coal India’s production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT)on a year-on-year basis in October, indicative of mining activity of the country’s largest producer picking up after being dampened because of monsoons.
The Kolkata-headquartered miner said that its supplies to the power sector also increased 19% to touch 57.1 MT. Overall supplies during the month surged 19% on a year-over-year basis to scale 70.3 MT. Both supplies to the power sector and overall supplies scaled record-highs in a single month, the company said.
About evacuation, it said that it loaded on an average 310 rakes per day — to the power sector — in October.
