briefs.headline: Commercial LPG price up 10, ATF 1.4 per litre
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Oil marketing companies Sunday increased the price of commercial LPG by Rs 10 for a 19-kg cylinder and hiked aviation turbine fuel (ATF) rates by Rs 1.37 per litre, in line with elevated international benchmarks, reports Atul Mathur.
A 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder used by hotels and restaurants will now cost Rs 2,820 in Delhi. ATF prices have risen to Rs 138.5 per litre. This is the third consecutive monthly increase in commercial LPG prices and the fourth straight monthly hike in ATF rates.
The price of commercial LPG varies across states due to differences in tax structures. A 19-kg cylinder will now cost Rs 2,775 in Mumbai, Rs 2,971 in Kolkata and Rs 2,994.50 in Chennai.
There has been no change in the price of the 14.2-kg domestic LPG cylinder, which continues to cost Rs 942 in Delhi. Petrol and diesel prices also remain unchanged.
ATF and LPG prices are revised on the first day of every month based on international benchmark prices and the rupee-dollar exchange rate.
International crude oil prices remained elevated through Oct, with Brent crude trading at $113.43 per barrel on Saturday. The Indian basket of crude oil averaged a record $119.96 per barrel in Oct.

briefs.headline: Government testing DigiYatra for international flights
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra. The govt has started trials for international passengers at seven airports, allowing eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.
Aviation ministry said trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. "Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, security hold areas and boarding gates, wherever required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027," it said in a statement. Another 25 Indian airports are planned to be covered by 2027.
To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based "verifiable credential" through Digi Yatra mobile app. "The process involves scanning machine readable zone of e-passport, reading embedded chip using the near field communication feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. 
The credential is stored in the passenger's Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials," the statement added.
The facility will complement, and not replace, existing processes. "Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities," it added.
IndiGo said eligible passengers can upload their boarding pass to Digi Yatra app. After completing document verification at check-in counter, they can proceed through the security hold area and boarding gates using Digi Yatra biometric face authentication.
"Interoperability with global frameworks such as IATA's One ID and ICAO's Public Key Directory will be an important part of this journey, helping explore how e-passport-based digital credentials can enable seamless journeys across borders, while keeping passenger consent and privacy central to experience," Digi Yatra Foundation CEO Suresh Khadakbhavi said.

briefs.headline: GST mop-up rises record 23% in Octoer, hits Rs 2.3 lakh crore
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: GST collections grew 22.9% in Oct – the fastest pace of expansion since the revamp of the tax regime in Sept 2025 – to reach Rs 2.3 lakh crore, the second-highest monthly mop-up since the rationalisation exercise. While consumption remains strong, the numbers indicate a bunching of quarter-end demand and the base effect as sales had slowed in Sept 2025 in anticipation of lower rates kicking in from Sept 22
The numbers for Oct 2026, based on transactions in Sept, pegged domestic GST collection growth at 15.8% to just under Rs 1.6 lakh crore, while integrated GST on imports jumped 42% to Rs 72,246 crore. Analysts see the increase in GST on imports as a result of higher commodity prices, although there was also a word of caution given that there has been a rising trend in recent months.
Refunds rose 6.5% to Rs 27,934 crore, and net collections were 25.6% higher at over Rs 2 lakh crore.
All states except four report higher GST collections, with Meghalaya and Himachal Pradesh leading growth.
“From the collections data for the month, it is possible to infer that: a) festival season consumption increases have started in a big way; b) focus on strict GST compliance and increasing GST audits is paying off and c) import GST is now a significant part of the overall collections, depicting a growing import driven consumption growth,” said MS Mani, partner at consulting firm Deloitte.
The current trends point to the Centre surpassing its GST collection target for the year, a positive for its finances amid higher subsidy outgo due to the war in West Asia. “While the Oct numbers are encouraging, the more important test will be whether this momentum continues after the festive season,” said Manot Mishra, partner and tax controversy management leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, a consulting firm.
Among the states, Meghalaya (32%) and Himachal Pradesh (30%) led the growth charts, with all states logging an increase, barring Jharkhand, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Among the large states, Uttar Pradesh reported a 20% rise in SGST mop-up in Oct, while Maharashtra (11%), Karnataka (16%), Tamil Nadu (8%) and Gujarat (18%).

briefs.headline: UPI crosses record 25 billion transactions
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: UPI transactions crossed the 25-billion mark for the first time in Oct, while average daily transaction value breached Rs 1 lakh crore for the first time, signalling continued growth in digital payments despite the debate over the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges.
UPI processed 25.5 billion transactions worth Rs 31.5 lakh crore in Oct, compared with 24.1 billion transactions valued at Rs 29.4 lakh crore in Sept. Transaction volumes rose 5.8% month on month, while the value of payments increased 7.4%.
The increase was also reflected in daily averages. Average daily transactions rose 2.5% to 822 million in Oct from 802 million in Sept, while average daily transaction value increased 3.9% to Rs 1,01,707 crore from Rs 97,913 crore. On a year-on-year basis, transaction volumes grew 23% in Oct, matching Sept's growth rate. However, value growth moderated to 16% from 18% in Sept.
The Oct numbers come amid a debate over the introduction of MDR charges, with some quarters raising concerns about the potential impact on merchant acceptance and cost of digital payments. The latest figures, however, show no immediate slowdown in aggregate UPI activity.

briefs.headline: Manufacturing divide: 10% factories account for 72% output
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's manufacturing sector suffers from fragmentation, with a small minority of large establishments driving output, while thousands of medium and small units are burdened with debt and low productivity.
Large factories, employing over 200 workers, account for 10.4% of total operational units, but generate nearly 72% of the country's manufacturing gross value added (GVA) amounting to Rs 15.9 lakh crore and provide 63% of industrial jobs.
In contrast, smaller factories, employing up to 50 workers, make up over 71% of all operational units but contribute 10% to overall manufacturing GVA. Units with up to 10 workers represent 36.3% of operational factories, but yield 2% of output, a recent study in a NSO journal, using data from the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2022-23, showed.
Large factories drive nearly 72% of manufacturing output despite making up just 10.4% of units
The GVA by the manufacturing sector in the country was estimated at around Rs 22 lakh crore in 2022-23. To accelerate industrial growth, policy experts frequently recommend facilitating the scaling up of smaller units through targeted technology upgradation, cluster-based supply chain linkages with larger firms, and easier credit access.
This productivity gap also coincides with a large debt burden on smaller establishments as factories with up to 10 workers carry a formal loan-to-GVA ratio of 85%, compared with around 39% for factories that have more than 200 workers. 
This indicates that while small units leverage significant formal credit relative to their size, low capacity utilisation and limited scale prevent them from translating that capital into proportionate output.
In terms of employing women workers, the ASI study underscores much sharper vulnerabilities on factory floors as merely 11% of the overall manufacturing workforce is female. The share rises marginally from 8.5% in factories employing up to 10 workers to 11.5% in large units with more than 200 workers.
A key driver behind the productivity divide is the sharp disparity in shop-floor enablers, such as research and development and worker training. Across all operating factories, a mere 2.7% maintain an active R&D unit, while only 6.7% provide formal skill training to workers. Adoption, however, the study finds, scales heavily with size. Nearly 12% large units operate R&D facilities and 20% offer formal training, compared to just 0.6% and 2.5% respectively among micro units (up to 10 workers).

briefs.headline: EV sales cross record 3.5 lakh units in October
briefs.bodyText:
CHENNAI: Amid festive fervour, India's electric vehicle (EV) market clocked a record month in Oct, with registrations crossing 3.5 lakh units for the first time.
Electric two-wheelers did most of the heavy lifting, notching up record sales and growing close to 50% year-on-year. Electric passenger vehicles (PVs) presented a more mixed picture: registrations jumped 75% year-on-year but fell 4% from Sept.
The final Oct tally could be higher, as there is typically a lag before all registrations are reflected on the Vahan dashboard. Even so, the figures available as of Nov 1 point to a landmark month for India's EV market.
Total EV registrations across all segments stood at about 3,54,000 units in Oct, compared with 2,45,000 units in Oct 2025 and 3,38,000 units in Sept this year.
EV registrations have now surpassed the 3-lakh mark for the fifth month in a row. Electric 2w registrations also hit a record high of 2,24,000 units in Oct, compared with 1,51,000 units in Oct 2025 and 2,09,000 units in Sept this year.

briefs.headline: LICHF bets on diversification to drive growth
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: LIC Housing Finance plans to grow faster than the market even as it improves its margin by changing the composition of its loan book. The company has increased its lending rate by 25 basis points to protect margins and plans to grow higher-margin loans against property (LAP), lease rental discounting (LRD) and project finance.
LICHF plans to have a dedicated affordable housing vertical in FY28 to manage the segment's smaller loans through closer monitoring and faster recovery. The move comes as Q2 NIM fell 4 basis points year-on-year to 2.58% as funding costs outpaced lending yields. Net profit rose 12% to Rs 1,506 crore, while disbursements grew 11% to Rs 18,127 crore.
Sandeep Kumar, MD & CEO, said that following the rate hike, about 35% of the portfolio will see the revision take effect from Nov 1, while the remaining 65% will be reset from Jan 1. Kumar said housing credit growth was showing signs of moderation in banks, reflecting caution amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties. However, he said underlying demand remained firm, with the industry continuing to see growth of 11% to 12%.

briefs.headline: Costlier phones give refurbished devices a boost
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Refurbished smartphones are finding more buyers in India. Rising prices of new devices are pushing consumers towards cheaper alternatives, including older iPhones, helping the secondary market grow even as new handset sales face a slowdown. ControlZ (refurbished electronics retailer) reported 100% growth this festive season, led by the iPhone 13, 14 and 15 series, founder and CEO Yug Bhatia, said. He identified the Rs 30,000-50,000 band as its strongest segment.
"When an entry-level Android phone costs about the same as a like-new iPhone, most buyers prefer the iPhone," Bhatia said.
He estimated India's pre-owned smartphone market at about 5 crore units, with iPhones accounting for 15-20%. Supply was sufficient, he said, but the largely unorganised market needed to be organised to bring renewed devices to more buyers in smaller towns.
Cashify, another refurbished electronics retailer, said sales of refurbished smartphones priced above Rs 50,000 more than doubled, while trade-ins in that segment more than quadrupled. Overall, exchange volumes rose 25%, with the average trade-in value reaching Rs 15,105. 
The company also reported stronger growth in smaller cities. Trade-ins in Tier 3 and beyond grew 49%, compared with 39% across the six metros. Motorola and Google recorded the fastest growth in upgrade and trade-in activity, at 79% and 74%, respectively, while Samsung led in overall volumes.
The shift is also visible in the models consumers are exchanging. Cashify said trade-in activity was increasingly moving towards newer devices, including the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, indicating that consumers were upgrading more frequently and looking to recover greater value from their existing smartphones. The trend comes as India's new smartphone market faces pressure from rising handset prices, making refurbished devices an increasingly attractive alternative for buyers looking for premium features at lower prices.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion; Max Verstappen wins in Mexico
stories.deck: Antonelli ‌celebrated his first F1 world championship at 20 years and 68 ‌days old, ⁠more than three years younger than Germany’s Sebastian Vettel when ⁠he set the previous record in 2010
stories.bodyText:
Kimi Antonelli was crowned the youngest-ever Formula 1 world champion on Sunday after the Italian star finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
That podium told the story of Formula 1’s recent past, present and future: Hamilton, the greatest driver of his generation with a record-tying seven drivers’ championships; Verstappen, who dominated the start of this decade with four consecutive titles from 2021-24; and Antonelli, who wrote his name in the record books thanks to nine wins and 16 podiums this year.
Antonelli has risen to 380 points with four races remaining. Verstappen (261) snuck past Hamilton (259) in the standings, but they will be racing for second the rest of the way.
Antonelli celebrated his first F1 world championship at 20 years and 68 days old, more than three years younger than Germany’s Sebastian Vettel when he set the previous record in 2010.
“It’s a day I will remember forever,” Antonelli said. “Thank you to my team, my family and everyone who supports me. It’s starting to feel real now, I’m going to enjoy every bit.
“We had such a strong car, and we were so consistent, I knew we had a chance. Just so glad we could finish it off.”
Verstappen crossed the finish line in 2:20:28.772, edging Hamilton by 0.799 seconds. The Red Bull Racing star has won three of the past four Grand Prix.
“I had a very good first lap,” Verstappen said. “We had a good strategy, I do think we lacked a little bit of pace but we hung in there.
“It was tough. I was sweating at the end to keep Lewis behind.”
The Dutchman was also among those who took time to congratulate Antonelli, who also became the first Italian world champion in 73 years.
“It is incredible, what a season (Antonelli) has had, and to do this at such an age ... I’m sure this is a very emotional day for him, and I am very proud of him,” Verstappen said.
Antonelli started the race in fourth and needed to finish ninth or better to secure the championship on Sunday no matter what his peers did. He had a relatively drama-free run, though the race was interrupted by a red flag around Lap 45 when Valtteri Bottas crashed.
Antonelli managed to pass Charles Leclerc for third around Lap 48, and the Mercedes driver was in fine shape the rest of the day.
“Without them I wouldn’t be here, without Mercedes and my family,” Antonelli said. “It’s a special moment and one that will live forever. I’m speechless, I’m trying to process what just happened.
“It’s been an incredible season, to share this podium with Max and Lewis is really incredible. I’m looking forward to more battles in the future.”
Mercedes now sits at 630 points in the constructors’ championship standings, a healthy 126-point lead over Ferrari.

stories.headline: Arsenal beats Liverpool to claim Premier League top spot
stories.deck: Kai Havertz scores only goal of the game as the champions claim first league victory at Anfield in 14 years
stories.bodyText:
Champions Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League with Kai Havertz's early goal securing a statement 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
German striker Havertz tapped in from Declan Rice's low cross in the 16th minute after the hosts were caught trying to play the ball out of their defence.
Liverpool responded strongly as halftime approached with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the crossbar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over the bar.
But Arsenal weathered the storm and defended superbly to keep Liverpool largely at arm's length after the break and seal their first Premier League win at Anfield for 14 years.
Mikel Arteta's side replaced Manchester City at the top with 24 points from nine games, with City on 21 after losing at home to Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday, their second successive league defeat after winning their first seven.
Liverpool's second league defeat of the season left them nine points behind Arsenal in fifth place.
For all Liverpool's huff and puff they failed to register an effort on target as Arsenal smothered their hosts with the kind of gritty away display that has become Arteta's blueprint.
'Crazy stat’
Arsenal were stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup in midweek but normal service was restored as they frustrated Liverpool to record a sixth clean sheet in nine league games and the significance of the win was clear in the way their players celebrated in front of their joyous fans.
"This means a lot to the whole football club and it's been 14 years, that is a crazy stat and I think that we are all happy that we gave it to them today," Havertz said.
"I think we all know what this stadium is about and what the fans are about. Liverpool have big players and they can show their quality. We knew that this was coming for us and we all stuck together and defended together."
Liverpool have slowly found their rhythm this season under Andoni Iraola and victory on Sunday would have raised hopes of them being genuine title contenders.
But after back-to-back league wins they got a reality check and could have few complaints.
Liverpool were architects of their own downfall as they ceded possession to Arsenal's press and when the ball was played out to Noni Madueke he found the overlapping Rice who slid a pass across for Havertz to end his nine-game goal drought.
Iraola's team dominated the rest of the half and had a strong penalty shout turned down when Jurrien Timber grabbed at Alexander Isak's shirt.
But Arsenal tightened up in the second half and denied the hosts any clear sights at goal.
"That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do and they just create waves and waves of attack. Relentless attacks," the tireless Rice said.
"We knew it wouldn't have been easy but in the end that defensive line and that togetherness is undefeated.
"So happy for Havertz because he deserved that goal and ultimately the 1-0 win."
Published - November 02, 2026 08:00 am IST

stories.headline: Two key players ruled out as New Zealand name updated ODI squad
stories.deck: New Zealand have suffered two injury setbacks ahead of their ODI series against India, with Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra ruled out. Chapman is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Ravindra is still struggling with a shoulder problem. Both players will miss the upcoming ODI series against India.
stories.bodyText:
New Zealand have suffered two injury setbacks ahead of their ODI series against India, with 
Mark Chapman
 and 
Rachin Ravindra
 ruled out. Chapman is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Ravindra is still struggling with a shoulder problem. Both players will miss the upcoming ODI series against India.
The New Zealand selectors have made changes to the squad, bringing in Henry Nicholls, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft and Tim Seifert.
Seifert, who was initially selected only for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will now be available for the entire series. Nicholls will join the squad for the first three matches, while Foxcroft will be part of the team for the final two games.
Nicholls earns call-up 
Nicholls has earned his place after scoring 119 for Canterbury in their second match against Wellington Firebirds. It was his 13th century in List A cricket. Foxcroft will join the New Zealand squad after completing the red-ball series against India A.
Matt Fisher, who was originally picked for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will also remain with the squad throughout the series as an additional bowling option.
Meanwhile, Matt Henry will join the team on Monday. His availability for the matches will depend on an assessment of his fitness.
Chapman and Ravindra need more time to recover
A recent MRI scan showed that Chapman needs another two weeks of rehabilitation before he can return to full fitness. Ravindra's right shoulder also needs more recovery time before he can field at full capacity.
New Zealand head coach Rob Walter said the absence of both players was disappointing.
“Everyone knows what an asset Mark and Rachin are to this side so it’s a shame they have to miss this series,” said Walter.
“I caught up with Mark last week and although he’s disappointed he’s working hard to get back on the field. With Rachin, his shoulder hasn’t quite recovered to a position where he could field comfortably in white-ball cricket, so with the Test series later this month we don’t want to take any undue risks. We’re pleased to bring in Henry who is no stranger to this side, and Dean who recently featured in the ODIs against the West Indies," he said.

stories.headline: IND A vs NZ A: Siraj, Mukesh run through New Zealand A batting
stories.bodyText:
Akash Deep is not pleased with the ball situation and has another discussion with the umpire, handing the ball back to him.
The Indian players appear to have convinced the umpire to make a change, with a replacement ball seemingly brought in.
However, Akash does not look satisfied. He is having a chat with umpire.
WICKET!
Mukesh Kumar strikes again to complete his five-wicket haul in the innings, his 12th in first-class cricket. He bowls a full delivery outside off that moves away, tempting Fraser Sheat into a drive.
The batter gets an edge and Devdutt Padikkal takes a comfortable catch at second slip. Sheat departs for 40 off 51 balls, bringing another useful lower-order contribution to an end.
Jayden Lennox pulls a short delivery from Mukesh Kumar towards backward square leg and picks up two runs. New Zealand A reach 346/8 in 105.4 overs, drawing level with India's first-innings total of 346.
The visitors have two wickets remaining.
WICKWT!
Mukesh Kumar strikes again to dismiss Kristian Clarke for 41, breaking New Zealand A's 47-run eighth-wicket partnership. Clarke pokes at a back-of-length delivery outside off that moves slightly away and gets an outside edge.
Smaran Ravichandran, who had dropped a catch earlier at first slip, makes no mistake this time and takes a comfortable catch.
Mukesh picks up his fourth wicket of the innings.
New Zealand A have reached 338/7 in 101.1 overs at the drinks break in the second session on Day 3. 
Kristian Clarke is batting on 41 off 66 balls, while Fraser Sheat has contributed an unbeaten 20 off 35 deliveries.
The pair have added 47 runs for the eighth wicket and brought New Zealand A within touching distance of India's first-innings total of 346.
DROPPED!
India A miss a golden opportunity to pick up another wicket as Smaran Ravichandran drops a regulation catch at first slip.
Fraser Sheat pokes at an Akash Deep delivery outside off and gets an edge that flies to the left of the slip fielder.
Smaran gets low and tries to grab it with both hands but fails to hold on. A big let-off for Sheat!
Mohammed Siraj strikes just before lunch, bowling Brett Randell for five to claim his fourth wicket of the innings. Randell looks to leave a length delivery outside off but misses it completely as the ball crashes into the top of off stump.
Siraj finishes the session in style, giving India A another boost. India A go into lunch on Day 3 as the happier side.
Mukesh Kumar strikes to give India A another breakthrough as Mitchell Hay departs for 31. Hay stays rooted to his crease and goes for a loose shot at a length delivery outside off.
He gets a thick edge, which Dhruv Jurel collects comfortably behind the stumps.
It is Mukesh's third wicket, taking both Indian pacers to three wickets each. India A are fighting back strongly.
Mohammed Siraj provides India A with another important breakthrough, dismissing Dean Foxcroft for 93. Bowling with the new ball, Siraj delivers a length ball that angles into the batter.
Foxcroft comes down the track and looks to play it on the leg side but misses the line and is struck on the pads. The umpire raises his finger after an LBW appeal.
Foxcroft is disappointed with the decision but has to walk back. New Zealand A lose their fifth wicket.
Mohammed Siraj provides India A with an early breakthrough on Day 3, ending Matthew Boyle's brilliant innings with a stunning catch from Devdutt Padikkal. Boyle edges a length delivery that moves slightly away from him.
Padikkal dives low to his left and pulls off a superb catch, with his fingers underneath the ball. Boyle departs for 110 off 152 balls, ending the 205-run fourth-wicket partnership.
With their team struggling, Boyle and Foxcroft showed patience and determination to rebuild the innings. They gradually settled down before taking on the Indian bowlers.
Boyle played an attacking knock to complete his century, while Foxcroft held one end together with a composed innings. Their partnership ensured New Zealand A did not lose another wicket before stumps.
Mukesh was India's most successful bowler, taking two wickets for 44 runs in 16 overs. Siraj finished with figures of 1/49 from 16 overs. Washington Sundar (14-1-44-0) and Akash Deep (11-2-35-0) went wicketless.
Earlier, India A were bowled out for 346 in their first innings, adding 55 runs to their overnight score of 291 for seven.
Captain Dhruv Jurel, who was unbeaten on 99 at the end of the opening day, completed his century before getting dismissed for 105. He faced 171 balls and hit 11 fours and three sixes.
Akash Deep also played an important innings, scoring 68 off 116 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes. His contribution helped India A cross the 300-run mark.
New Zealand A had a disastrous start to their innings, losing three wickets in the first eight overs to slip to 13 for three.
Mohammed Siraj provided the first breakthrough by dismissing captain Rhys Mariu for four. Dhruv Jurel took the catch behind the wickets.
Mukesh Kumar then struck twice in quick succession, removing Curtis Heaphy (4) and Tim Robinson (3) to put the hosts under pressure.
New Zealand A fought back strongly after a poor start to reach 218 for three at stumps on day two of the second unofficial Test against India A on Sunday. An unbeaten century from Matthew Boyle and a half-century by Dean Foxcroft helped the hosts recover from 13 for three.
Boyle was unbeaten on 107 off 148 balls, hitting 14 fours and a six. Foxcroft was batting on 80 off 180 deliveries, with nine boundaries. The duo added an unbroken 205-run partnership for the fourth wicket to bring New Zealand A back into the contest.

briefs.headline: Kimi Antonelli creates history, becomes youngest F1 world champion
briefs.deck: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli made history on Sunday by becoming the youngest Formula One world champion at the age of 20. Antonelli secured the title after finishing third in a dramatic Mexico City Grand Prix, which was won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
briefs.bodyText:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli made history on Sunday by becoming the youngest Formula One world champion at the age of 20. Antonelli secured the title after finishing third in a dramatic Mexico City Grand Prix, which was won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
The Italian driver broke down in tears of joy over the team radio as he crossed the finish line. His lead in the championship standings has now reached an unbeatable 119 points.
The race at the high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was stopped by a red flag before being restarted.
Antonelli becomes first Italian champion since 1953
Antonelli also became the first Italian driver to win the Formula One world championship since 1953.
Despite missing out on the race victory, his third-place finish was enough to seal the title and put his name in the history books.
Dramatic race in Mexico City
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton started the race from pole position and finished second, just behind Verstappen.
The race was full of drama, with two safety cars and several crashes. The action was also interrupted by a 33-minute stoppage after a red flag with 25 of the 71 laps still remaining.

briefs.headline: 'Sanju mera first-choice': Ashwin comes to Samson's defence after New Zealand series struggles, delivers witty response
briefs.deck: Sanju Samson's performance in the T20I series against New Zealand raised eyebrows, as he could only amass 67 runs over five encounters. His struggles culminated in just four runs during the final match, prompting discussions about alternatives like Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Ravichandran Ashwin lightheartedly responded to critiques on social media. After initially leading 3-0, India concluded the…
briefs.bodyText:
Sanju Samson may have endured a difficult T20I series against New Zealand, but 
Ravichandran Ashwin
 was not going to let another round of criticism pass without a cheeky comeback. The former India spinner took a playful swipe at a social media user who questioned his continued backing of the wicketkeeper-batter following another low score in the fifth T20I on Sunday.
Samson's struggles continued in the series decider as he was dismissed for just four runs. A social media user then attempted to draw Ashwin into the debate, pointing to the batter's disappointing run and questioning his support for him.
"Hello Ashwin, your first choice Sanju flopped throughout the entire series @ashwinravi99," the user wrote.
Ashwin responded with a witty one-liner that quickly caught attention: "Sanju mera first-choice, tumhara full-time obsession (Sanju is my first choice, he's your full-time obsession)."
Samson's lean run sparks selection debate
Samson's scores across the five-match series read 67, 14, 18, 4 and 4. After making a promising start with a half-century in the opening T20I, the right-hander struggled to build on it, managing only 40 runs across his final four outings.
His inconsistent returns have fuelled debate on social media over whether India should consider giving young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi an extended opportunity at the top of the order.
Sooryavanshi featured in two matches during the series, scoring four and 45. His aggressive approach and promising knock have added another dimension to the selection discussion, although the teenager is still at an early stage of his international career.
How India fared in the five-match series
India began the series strongly, winning the first three matches to take an unassailable 3-0 lead. New Zealand responded by winning the fourth and fifth T20Is to finish the series on a high, reducing the final margin to 3-2.

briefs.headline: Lifter Usha tops her 61kg group, Nirupama finishes disappointing 4th in Group C at World Championships
briefs.deck: Following the completion of Groups C and D, Usha was placed third overall while Nirupama was fifth
briefs.bodyText:
Indian weightlifter Usha topped Group D, while compatriot Nirupama Devi endured a disappointing outing to finish fourth in Group C of the women's 61kg competition at the IWF World Championships in Ningbo on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The 23-year-old Usha lifted a total of 212kg — 93kg in snatch and 119kg in clean and jerk — to finish ahead of all the lifters in her group and several competitors in the higher Group C as well.
Nirupama, who has moved down from the 63kg weight class, managed a total of 211kg (91kg+120kg), one kilogram short of Usha's effort despite being placed in Group C owing to her higher entry total.
Following the completion of Groups C and D, Usha was placed third overall while Nirupama was fifth.
Their final standings will be updated after the completion of Group A.
Usha started with a successful 90kg snatch before failing to lift 93kg in her next attempt, but the Indian regained her composure to clear the same weight in her third and final snatch attempt.
In the clean and jerk as well, Usha managed to complete two of her three attempts. After successfully lifting 115kg and 119kg, she faltered in her final attempt of 121kg.
On the other hand, Nirupama just managed to register a total after completing the minimum two successful lifts.
She started with a failed attempt at 91kg in snatch but managed to lift the weight in her second attempt before failing to clear 93kg in her third.
In the clean and jerk, she lifted 120kg before failing in both attempts to heave 124kg.
At the World Championships, Group A comprises lifters with the highest declared entry totals — the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk — while Groups B, C and D feature athletes with progressively lower entry totals.
The World Championships is one of six events in the first period of the Olympic qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

briefs.headline: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stand on brink of MotoGP world title
briefs.deck: Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season
briefs.bodyText:
Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth world title with an imperious victory at the Malaysian MotoGP on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The Ducati star romped to a dominant win in 40min 14.236sec, finishing 4.172sec ahead of Red Bull’s Pedro Acosta as his younger brother Alex Marquez came third, almost six seconds adrift.
Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season.
It was also his third triumph in Malaysia in the MotoGP class, having last won in Sepang back in 2018.
With Aprilia’s Martin missing the Sepang weekend with a broken wrist, his fellow Spaniard Marquez can seal the championship next weekend in Qatar.
Marquez wasted no time in snatching the lead from his brother as the riders came into Turn 1 from the start, and the siblings briefly traded places before the older Marquez just edged ahead in scorching conditions.
Saturday’s sprint race winner Acosta tailed both the Marquez brothers closely in third, with Italian Marco Bezzecchi in fourth and Japan’s Ai Ogura in fifth.
Championship leader Marquez, 33, began to pull away from the chasing pack to develop a 1.7 sec advantage over his brother, who was valiantly defending his second spot against Acosta.
Acosta would be rewarded for his persistence as the Red Rull rider snatched second place from Alex Marquez in Lap 10.
At the front Marquez coasted to victory unchallenged to continue his purple streak in the second half of the 2026 season.
After Qatar there are just two weekends left in the campaign.

briefs.headline: Alcaraz beats De Minaur to win Vienna Open without dropping a set to clinch fourth title this year
briefs.deck: Carlos Alcaraz has beaten Alex de Minaur on grass and clay as well as on indoor and outdoor hard courts
briefs.bodyText:
Seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and defeat his opponent for the seventh time in as many meetings.
Alcaraz has beaten the Australian on grass and clay as well as on indoor and outdoor hard courts.
He sealed his latest victory with trademark panache.
Alcaraz drew his opponent to the net with a sliced backhand drop shot. De Minaur retrieved it but Alcaraz lobbed him with a backhand and, after the Australian volleyed that shot back near the net, clipped a cross-court forehand that landed just in.
The second-seeded Spaniard looked jubilant and cracked a broad smile after clinching his fourth title this year — including the Australian Open for a career Grand Slam — and his 28th overall.
The fifth-seeded De Minaur was looking for his second title of the year.
He advanced to the final of the ATP 500 event with a semifinal win against Alexander Zverev, who will top the rankings on Monday (November 2, 2026). Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev in the other semi.

briefs.headline: ISL: Gritty Delhi rallies to beat Mumbai
briefs.deck: Carlos Fortes (73), Akshat Mehra (90+2) and Juan Pena (90+4) were on target for Delhi, which had trailed 0-2 at the break following goals from Muhammad Ajsal (6) and Zothanpuia (27)
briefs.bodyText:
SC Delhi netted three times in the final 20 minutes to beat Mumbai City FC 3-2 in an Indian Super League fixture in Mumbai on Sunday (November, 1, 2026).
Carlos Fortes (73), Akshat Mehra (90+2) and Juan Pena (90+4) were on target for the visitor, which had trailed 0-2 at the break following goals from Muhammad Ajsal (6) and Zothanpuia (27).
The host took the lead as Ajsal played a superb one-two with Noufal before slotting home following a defensive error from Lamgoulen Hangshing.
Mumbai doubled its advantage in the 27th minute. Noufal made a strong run down the left before crossing for Zothanpuia, who calmly finished with his right foot.
In the 73rd minute, T.P. Rehenesh spilled a corner, and the ball fell to Ashutosh Mehta, who set up Fortes for a tap-in to reduce the deficit.
Substitute Mehra made an immediate impact, taking a pass from Richard Ndayishimaye into his stride and curling an effort at Rehenesh, who could only push the ball into his own net.
Only minutes later, Pena completed the turnaround, sprinting forward in the 94th minute and dancing his way past two Mumbai City defenders before slotting homel.
